items.title: Outcomes of School-Based Mental Health Screening Programs: A Systematic Review

ai.headline: School mental health screening helps spot students who need support and increases service use, but effects on symptoms and grades are uncertain.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 22 studies of school-based mental health screening for children and adolescents aged 5–18. Screening consistently improved identification of mental health needs and was generally linked to greater use of mental health services, but effects on anxiety and depressive symptoms were inconsistent, and evidence on academic outcomes was limited and mixed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that schools can help find young people who might otherwise miss out on mental health support, though screening alone does not guarantee better symptoms or school results.
ai.life_skill: Notice if you or a friend are struggling and speak to a trusted adult or school staff member so help can be arranged.
ai.fact: School-based screening is consistently linked to better identification of students with mental health needs and greater use of mental health services.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the effect of school-based screening on anxiety and depressive symptoms?
quiz.answer: Effects on anxiety and depressive symptoms were inconsistent, and several trials found no between-group difference.

ai.caveat: Study quality was not formally appraised and designs, screening tools, and outcome measures varied widely, so findings should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults With Cancer and Their Parents and for Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults Affected by Parental Cancer: A Population-Stratified Systematic Review.

ai.headline: ACT may reduce distress and anxiety in parents of young people with cancer, but evidence for young people themselves is weak.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at nine studies involving 573 people to see if acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) helps children, adolescents, young adults with cancer, those affected by parental cancer, and their parents. It found moderate-certainty evidence that ACT reduced distress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms in parents, while evidence for young people was of very low certainty.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a specific talking therapy can support the mental health of parents caring for a young person with cancer, while highlighting that more research is needed for the young people themselves.
ai.life_skill: Notice when difficult thoughts or feelings show up and try to acknowledge them without judging yourself.
ai.fact: Psychological flexibility was identified as a possible factor behind quality-of-life improvements in one study of distressed adolescents and young adults affected by their own or a family member's cancer.

quiz.question: Which group showed moderate-certainty reductions in distress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms from ACT?
quiz.answer: Parents of children, adolescents, and young adults with cancer.

ai.caveat: The findings for young people are based on very low-certainty evidence and a mix of weak study designs, so they are not proof that ACT works for them.

ai.summary: The paper reviews current global approaches to AI safety and governance and identifies key issues such as safety, inclusiveness, accountability, coordination and effective governance. items.title: Effects of infertility on relationship quality and mental health outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review

ai.headline: Infertility is linked to poorer mental health and lower relationship quality in sub-Saharan Africa.
ai.summary: A scoping review of 70 studies looked at how infertility affects people in sub-Saharan Africa. It found infertility is linked to anxiety, depression, emotional distress, isolation, grief, and lower relationship quality, including abuse, infidelity, and separation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how social pressure around having children can affect relationships and mental wellbeing, highlighting the need for better support.
ai.life_skill: Notice if someone you know is struggling with infertility and offer non-judgmental support rather than pressure or blame.
ai.fact: Infertility is associated with anxiety, depression, emotional distress, isolation, and grief over unfulfilled reproductive goals.

quiz.question: What did the review find about infertility and relationship quality?
quiz.answer: Diminished relationship quality was common, including intimate partner violence, verbal and emotional abuse, loss of intimacy, infidelity, and separation or divorce.

ai.caveat: A scoping review maps existing evidence but does not prove cause and effect, and the included studies vary in design and quality.

items.title: Physical activity intervention for blood pressure reduction in low and middle-income countries: a systematic review with meta-analysis

ai.headline: Structured physical activity programmes lower blood pressure in adults with hypertension in low- and middle-income countries.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 45 studies of adults with high blood pressure in low- and middle-income countries who took part in physical activity programmes. Compared with control groups, office systolic blood pressure fell by about 10 mmHg and diastolic by about 5 mmHg, though effects varied across settings.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that exercise can be a practical way to help manage high blood pressure in many parts of the world.
ai.life_skill: Try building regular physical activity into your routine if you have high blood pressure, after checking with a health professional.
ai.fact: Physical activity interventions reduced office systolic blood pressure by an average of 10.23 mmHg compared with control in chronic controlled trials.

quiz.question: By how much did physical activity reduce office systolic blood pressure compared with control in chronic controlled trials?
quiz.answer: It reduced it by an average of 10.23 mmHg.

ai.caveat: The evidence is mainly from office blood pressure readings, with limited data on 24-hour ambulatory monitoring and long-term community programmes, and results varied across studies.

items.title: An impact assessment of a reading and writing instruction method in a socially vulnerable context

ai.headline: A Spanish early literacy program improved reading and writing skills in young children from vulnerable backgrounds.
ai.summary: The study tested the Sophia Method, which teaches linguistic, metalinguistic, and graphomotor skills, with 280 Uruguayan preschool and first-grade students from socioeconomically vulnerable schools. Children in the intervention group showed higher adjusted posttest performance across all three educational levels compared to a comparison group, with larger gains for some students who started with lower pretest scores.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how structured early literacy teaching can support children facing socioeconomic disadvantage.

ai.caveat: The study used a quasi-experimental design rather than random assignment, so it cannot prove the method caused the improvements.

items.title: The Effectiveness of Local-Level Food Environment Policies in Improving Diet Quality of Socioeconomically Disadvantaged Population Groups. A Systematic Literature Review.

ai.headline: Local food policies can modestly improve diet quality for disadvantaged groups, especially with financial incentives and combined approaches.
ai.summary: This systematic review examined 77 studies covering 104 local government food environment policies, mostly in US municipalities, aimed at improving diet quality among socioeconomically disadvantaged people. It found that effectiveness was generally modest or mixed, with economic incentives and combined environmental-behavioural approaches showing the most consistent benefits, while isolated infrastructure or labelling policies had limited impact.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how local rules about food shops, prices and provision can shape everyday eating, especially for people on low incomes.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether local food schemes offer financial incentives or combine several changes, as these are more likely to help improve diet quality.
ai.fact: Economic incentives and combined environmental-behavioural food policies produced the most consistent dietary gains among disadvantaged groups.
ai.caveat: The included studies had risk of bias, vague outcome evaluation, and resource constraints affecting sustainability, so findings should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.

items.title: A Local Enrichment Computational Framework to Identify Disease-Enriched Physical Activity Patterns

ai.headline: A new computer method finds activity patterns linked to diseases using wearable tracker data.
ai.summary: Researchers developed LocPA, a framework that analyses 24-hour accelerometer data to find physical activity patterns enriched in specific diseases. Applied to UK Biobank data across six diseases, it found two common patterns: low daytime activity and disrupted sleep with elevated nighttime activity, with the latter linked to worse health in hypertension and diabetes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how wearable data might one day help spot disease-related behaviour patterns that standard activity summaries miss.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your own activity is mostly low during the day or includes lots of nighttime movement, and discuss any concerns with a health professional.
ai.fact: Two recurring activity patterns—low daytime activity and sleep disruption with elevated nighttime activity—appeared across six different disease groups.

quiz.question: What two activity patterns did LocPA find across six diseases?
quiz.answer: A low-activity phenotype with reduced daytime activity and a sleep-disrupted phenotype with reduced daytime and elevated nocturnal activity.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the findings are observational so they show links, not proof of cause and effect.

items.title: Tracking vocabulary development as children start school: assessing measurement invariance in multilingual classrooms

ai.summary: Researchers tracked 1,949 test administrations from children aged four to nine across 40 schools over one academic year. ai.why_it_matters: It shows how a vocabulary test can be checked for fairness so children with different language experiences can be compared over time.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether a test or measure treats people from different backgrounds fairly before trusting its results.
ai.fact: Receptive vocabulary—understanding words when hearing them—underpins reading comprehension and wider learning.

quiz.answer: Between-group differential item functioning effects were small to negligible.

items.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution

ai.summary: Researchers built ProTEUS, a model that learns from protein mutation data and predicts how changes affect protein function. It was tested in two lab campaigns and produced variants with more than ten times the activity of the original proteins.
